newsitem.title: USA: Talk of imminent tax deal optimistic - White House.
newsitem.headline: Talk of imminent tax deal optimistic - White House.

text.p: White House spokesman Mike McCurry said that it was "very optimistic" to expect the White House and congressional Republicans to come to a tax deal next week.
Asked at his midday briefing if reports that the two sides might come to an agreement next week were reasonable, McCurry replied: "I think they're very optimistic."

McCurry said the White House was building support for its position that parts of the Senate and House-passed tax cut packages needed to be restructured, and indicated that this process was still far from complete.

The White House has said certain provisions of both bills are unacceptable, but has carefully avoided threatening veto. McCurry again shied away from such a threat when asked about a Republican plan, called "stacking," to strip tax credits from some low-income workers.
"We expect it will change before there's a final vote," he said.
